metadata.title: Benign Overfitting in Linear Regression
metadata.authors: Peter L. Bartlett, Philip M. Long, Gábor Lugosi, Alexander Tsigler

nodes.name: Linear regression problem
nodes.statement: A linear regression problem in a separable Hilbert space $\bbH$ is defined by random covariate $x\in\bbH$ and outcome $y\in\Re$, with covariance operator $\Sigma=\E[xx^\top]$ and optimal parameter $\theta^*=\arg\min_\theta \E(y-x^\top\theta)^2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Linear regression in a separable Hilbert space, with covariance operator and optimal parameter.

nodes.name: Standing assumptions on $(x,y)$
nodes.statement: (A1) $x,y$ mean zero; (A2) $x=V\Lambda^{1/2}z$ with $z$ having independent $\sigma_x^2$-subgaussian components; (A3) conditional noise variance $\E[(y-x^\top\theta^*)^2|x]\geq\sigma^2$; (A4) $y-x^\top\theta^*$ is $\sigma_y^2$-subgaussian conditionally on $x$; (A5) almost surely the projection of $X$ on the orthogonal complement of any eigenvector of $\Sigma$ spans dimension $n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Five assumptions on the data distribution: zero mean, subgaussian decomposition, lower-bounded noise, subgaussian noise, and a full-rank projection condition.
conclusions: Projection of $X$ on $v^\perp$ spans dimension $n$ a.s.

nodes.name: Minimum norm estimator
nodes.statement: Given $X\in\bbH^n$, $\bs{y}\in\Re^n$, the minimum norm estimator solves $\hat\theta=\arg\min_\theta\{\|\theta\|^2:\|X\theta-\bs{y}\|^2=\min_\beta\|X\beta-\bs{y}\|^2\}$, equivalently $\hat\theta=X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}\bs{y}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest-norm parameter that interpolates the training data.

nodes.name: Effective ranks $r_k(\Sigma)$ and $R_k(\Sigma)$
nodes.statement: For eigenvalues $\lambda_i=\mu_i(\Sigma)$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i<\infty$ and $\lambda_{k+1}>0$: $r_k(\Sigma)=\frac{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i}{\lambda_{k+1}}$ and $R_k(\Sigma)=\frac{(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i)^2}{\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i^2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two notions of effective rank built from tail eigenvalue sums.

nodes.name: Closed form of minimum norm estimator
nodes.statement: $\hat\theta = X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}\bs{y}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Pseudoinverse formula for the minimum norm interpolant.

nodes.name: Excess risk $R(\theta)$
nodes.statement: $R(\theta):=\E_{x,y}[(y-x^\top\theta)^2-(y-x^\top\theta^*)^2]$, the conditional expected gap to the Bayes risk given the estimator.
nodes.statement_clean: Excess prediction error of an estimator over the optimum.

nodes.name: Benign covariance sequence $\Sigma_n$
nodes.statement: A sequence $\Sigma_n$ is benign if $\lim_n r_0(\Sigma_n)/n = \lim_n k_n^*/n = \lim_n n/R_{k_n^*}(\Sigma_n) = 0$, where $k_n^*=\min\{k\geq 0:r_k(\Sigma_n)\geq bn\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic regime in which the minimum norm interpolant's excess risk vanishes.

nodes.name: Main characterization of benign overfitting
nodes.statement: For any $\sigma_x$ there exist $b,c,c_1>1$ such that: with $k^*=\min\{k\geq 0:r_k(\Sigma)\geq bn\}$, if $k^*\geq n/c_1$ then $\E R(\hat\theta)\geq\sigma^2/c$; otherwise w.p. $\geq 1-\delta$, $R(\hat\theta)\leq c(\|\theta^*\|^2\|\Sigma\|\max\{\sqrt{r_0/n},r_0/n,\sqrt{\log(1/\delta)/n}\})+c\log(1/\delta)\sigma_y^2(k^*/n+n/R_{k^*})$, with matching lower bound $\E R(\hat\theta)\geq(\sigma^2/c)(k^*/n+n/R_{k^*})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tight finite-sample upper and lower bounds on the excess risk of the minimum norm interpolant in terms of $r_0$, $k^*$ and $R_{k^*}$.
assumptions: Linear regression problem from Definition $\ref{def:linreg}$ (DP450.1, AssumP450.1)
conclusions: There exists $\theta^*$ with $\|\theta^*\|=t$ giving $R(\hat\theta)\geq \frac{1}{a_1}\|\theta^*\|^2\|\Sigma\| \ind[r_0/(n\log(1+r_0))\geq a_2]$ w.p. $\geq 1/4$

nodes.name: Effective rank ordering
nodes.statement: $r_k(\Sigma)\geq 1$, $r_k^2(\Sigma)=r_k(\Sigma^2)R_k(\Sigma)$, and $r_k(\Sigma^2)\leq r_k(\Sigma)\leq R_k(\Sigma)\leq r_k^2(\Sigma)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Order relations between the two notions of effective rank.
assumptions: $\Sigma$ is a covariance operator with summable eigenvalues

nodes.name: Eigenvalue patterns for benign overfitting
nodes.statement: (1) If $\mu_k(\Sigma)=k^{-\alpha}\ln^{-\beta}(k+1)$, then $\Sigma$ is benign iff $\alpha=1$ and $\beta>1$. (2) If $\mu_k(\Sigma_n)=\gamma_k+\epsilon_n$ for $k\leq p_n$ with $\gamma_k=\Theta(\exp(-k/\tau))$, then $\Sigma_n$ is benign iff $p_n=\omega(n)$ and $ne^{-o(n)}=\epsilon_n p_n=o(n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Examples showing infinite-dimensional benign overfitting requires $\alpha=1, \beta>1$ decay; finite-dimensional case admits arbitrarily slow decay with isotropic noise.
assumptions: $\Sigma$ or $\Sigma_n$ as defined in each case

nodes.name: Bias-variance decomposition (informal)
nodes.statement: $R(\hat\theta)\leq 2{\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*+c\sigma^2\log(1/\delta)\tr(C)$ w.p. $\geq 1-\delta$ over $\eps$, and $\E_\eps R(\hat\theta)\geq{\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*+\sigma^2\tr(C)$, where $B=(I-X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}X)\Sigma(I-X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}X)$ and $C=(XX^\top)^{-1}X\Sigma X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Decomposes excess risk into a bias term ${\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*$ and a noise/trace term involving $\tr(C)$.
assumptions: Setting of DP450.1, AssumP450.1; $\hat\theta$ from DP450.2

nodes.name: Subgaussian representation of $\tr(C)$
nodes.statement: With $z_i=Xv_i/\sqrt{\lambda_i}$ for eigenvectors $v_i$ of $\Sigma$ with $\lambda_i>0$, $\tr(C)=\sum_i\lambda_i^2 z_i^\top(\sum_j\lambda_j z_j z_j^\top)^{-2}z_i = \sum_i\lambda_i^2 z_i^\top A_{-i}^{-2}z_i / (1+\lambda_i z_i^\top A_{-i}^{-1}z_i)^2$, where $A_{-i}=\sum_{j\neq i}\lambda_j z_j z_j^\top$ and the $z_i$ are independent $\sigma_x^2$-subgaussian.
nodes.statement_clean: Re-expresses $\tr(C)$ in terms of independent unit-variance subgaussian vectors.

nodes.name: Proof of subgaussian representation
nodes.statement: Use the eigenbasis $Xv_i=\sqrt{\lambda_i}z_i$ to expand $XX^\top$ and $X\Sigma X^\top$, then apply Lemma SMW (Lemma $\ref{lemma::SMW_formula}$) with $k=1$.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue concentration for $A_k$
nodes.statement: There is $c$ such that for any $k\geq 0$, w.p. $\geq 1-2e^{-n/c}$: $\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i - c\lambda_{k+1}n \leq \mu_n(A_k)\leq \mu_1(A_k)\leq c(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i+\lambda_{k+1}n)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Concentration of extreme eigenvalues of the truncated weighted Wishart-like matrix.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of truncated $A_k$, $A_{-i}$, $A$
nodes.statement: With $b,c\geq 1$, w.p. $\geq 1-2e^{-n/c}$: (i) $\mu_{k+1}(A_{-i})\leq\mu_{k+1}(A)\leq\mu_1(A_k)\leq c(\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j+\lambda_{k+1}n)$; (ii) for $1\leq i\leq k$, $\mu_n(A)\geq\mu_n(A_{-i})\geq\mu_n(A_k)\geq\frac{1}{c}\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j-c\lambda_{k+1}n$; (iii) if $r_k(\Sigma)\geq bn$, $\frac{1}{c}\lambda_{k+1}r_k(\Sigma)\leq\mu_n(A_k)\leq\mu_1(A_k)\leq c\lambda_{k+1}r_k(\Sigma)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Extends the concentration to $A_{-i}$ and $A$, and shows that once $r_k\geq bn$ all eigenvalues of $A_k$ are within a constant factor.

nodes.name: Proof of LP450.5
nodes.statement: Combine LP450.4 with rank-$k$ argument and Courant-Fischer-Weyl monotonicity (LP450.20). For (iii), use $r_k\geq bn$ to bound $\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j+\lambda_{k+1}n\leq(1+1/b)\lambda_{k+1}r_k(\Sigma)$.

nodes.name: Upper bound on $\tr(C)$
nodes.section: 4.3 Upper bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: There are $b,c\geq 1$ such that if $0\leq k\leq n/c$, $r_k(\Sigma)\geq bn$, and $l\leq k$, then w.p. $\geq 1-7e^{-n/c}$: $\tr(C)\leq c(l/n + n\sum_{i>l}\lambda_i^2/(\sum_{i>k}\lambda_i)^2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: High-probability upper bound on the trace term in terms of $l/n$ and a tail eigenvalue ratio.

nodes.name: Proof of LP450.6
nodes.section: 4.3 Upper bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: Split $\tr(C)$ at index $l$ via LP450.3, bound each piece using LP450.5 (eigenvalue control of $A_{-i}, A$), Corollary CP450.1 (norms of subgaussian projections), and Bernstein-type Lemma LP450.7.

nodes.name: Weighted subexponential Bernstein bound
nodes.section: 4.3 Upper bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: For non-increasing summable $\{\lambda_i\}$ and independent centered $\sigma$-subexponential $\{\xi_i\}$, w.p. $\geq 1-2e^{-t}$: $|\sum_i \lambda_i \xi_i|\leq a\sigma\max(t\lambda_1,\sqrt{t\sum_i\lambda_i^2})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Bernstein-style tail bound for weighted sums of subexponentials.

nodes.name: Norm of subgaussian projection
nodes.section: 4.3 Upper bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: For centered $z\in\Re^n$ with independent $\sigma^2$-subgaussian unit-variance coordinates, and a random subspace $\Ls$ of codimension $k$ independent of $z$: w.p. $\geq 1-3e^{-t}$, $\|z\|^2\leq n+a\sigma^2(t+\sqrt{nt})$ and $\|\Pi_\Ls z\|^2\geq n-a\sigma^2(k+t+\sqrt{nt})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Concentration bounds on norm and projection of a subgaussian vector.
assumptions: $\Ls$ is a random subspace of codimension $k$ independent of $z$

nodes.name: Single-term lower bound on $\tr(C)$
nodes.section: 4.4 Lower bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: There is $c$ such that for any $i\geq 1$ with $\lambda_i>0$ and any $0\leq k\leq n/c$, w.p. $\geq 1-5e^{-n/c}$: $\frac{\lambda_i^2 z_i^\top A_{-i}^{-2}z_i}{(1+\lambda_i z_i^\top A_{-i}^{-1}z_i)^2}\geq \frac{1}{cn}\left(1+\frac{\sum_{j>k}\lambda_j+n\lambda_{k+1}}{n\lambda_i}\right)^{-2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-term lower bound for the components of $\tr(C)$, valid regardless of $r_k(\Sigma)$.
conclusions: Lower bound on the per-index summand of $\tr(C)$

nodes.name: Aggregation of high-probability lower bounds
nodes.section: 4.4 Lower bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: If $\{\eta_i\}$ are non-negative with $\Pr(\eta_i>t_i)\geq 1-\delta$ for each $i$, and at least one $t_i>0$, then $\Pr(\sum_i\eta_i\geq\frac12\sum_i t_i)\geq 1-2\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sums of pointwise high-probability lower bounds aggregate with at most a doubling of the failure probability.
assumptions: Non-negative reals $\{t_i\}$ with at least one strictly positive

nodes.name: Lower bound on $\tr(C)$
nodes.section: 4.4 Lower bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: There is $c$ such that for any $0\leq k\leq n/c$ and any $b>1$, w.p. $\geq 1-10e^{-n/c}$: (1) if $r_k(\Sigma)<bn$ then $\tr(C)\geq(k+1)/(cb^2 n)$; (2) if $r_k(\Sigma)\geq bn$ then $\tr(C)\geq\frac{1}{cb^2}\min_{l\leq k}(l/n+b^2 n\sum_{i>l}\lambda_i^2/(\lambda_{k+1}r_k(\Sigma))^2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: High-probability lower bound on $\tr(C)$ in two regimes of $r_k(\Sigma)$.
conclusions: Case $r_k\geq bn$: variational lower bound matching LP450.6 up to constants

nodes.name: Proof of LP450.10
nodes.section: 4.4 Lower bound on the trace term
nodes.statement: Apply LP450.3 and LP450.8 to give per-term lower bounds, then aggregate via LP450.9 and split into the two regimes.

nodes.name: Best choice of $l$
nodes.statement: For any $b\geq 1$ and $k^*=\min\{k:r_k(\Sigma)\geq bn\}$ with $k^*<\infty$: $\min_{l\leq k^*}(l/(bn)+bn\sum_{i>l}\lambda_i^2/(\lambda_{k^*+1}r_{k^*}(\Sigma))^2)= k^*/(bn)+bn/R_{k^*}(\Sigma)$.
nodes.statement_clean: The minimizer $l=k^*$ collapses the variational bound to the closed form $k^*/(bn)+bn/R_{k^*}(\Sigma)$.

nodes.name: Proof of TP450.1 (main theorem)
nodes.statement: Combine LP450.2 with the bias bound LP450.13 (Appendix) and the trace bounds LP450.6 / LP450.10 / LP450.11; the second paragraph (lower bound) is proved in Appendix $\ref{a:packing}$ via the packing argument LP450.18 + LP450.19.

nodes.name: Decompose excess risk via Lemma bv
nodes.statement: Apply LP450.2 to bound $R(\hat\theta)$ by ${\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*$ plus a multiple of $\sigma^2\log(1/\delta)\tr(C)$.

nodes.name: Bound bias term via LP450.13
nodes.statement: Use Lemma LP450.13 (Appendix $\ref{a:upperB}$) to show ${\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*\leq c\|\theta^*\|^2\|\Sigma\|\max\{\sqrt{r_0/n},r_0/n,\sqrt{t/n}\}$.

nodes.name: Case $k^*\geq n/c_1$: lower bound $\tr(C)$
nodes.statement: If no $k\leq n/c$ satisfies $r_k\geq bn$, then by LP450.10 part (1), $\tr(C)=\Omega(1)$, hence $\E R(\hat\theta)=\Omega(\sigma^2)$.

nodes.name: Case $k^*<n/c_1$: match upper and lower trace bounds
nodes.statement: Combine LP450.6 and LP450.10 part (2) to sandwich $\tr(C)$ around $\min_{l\leq k^*}(l/n+n\sum_{i>l}\lambda_i^2/(\lambda_{k^*+1}r_{k^*}(\Sigma))^2)$.

nodes.name: Collapse to closed form via LP450.11
nodes.statement: Apply LP450.11 to express the variational bound as $k^*/n+n/R_{k^*}(\Sigma)$.

nodes.name: Conclude upper and lower bounds for $R(\hat\theta)$
nodes.statement: Combining the bias bound (PSP450.2) and the trace bound (PSP450.5) finishes the first paragraph; the second paragraph follows from the packing argument in Appendix $\ref{a:packing}$.

nodes.name: Bias-variance decomposition (Appendix)
nodes.section: Appendix A: Proof of Lemma bv
nodes.statement: For the minimum norm estimator $\hat\theta$, $R(\hat\theta)=\E_x(x^\top(\theta^*-\hat\theta))^2\leq 2{\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*+2\bs{\eps}^\top C\bs{\eps}$ and $\E_{x,\eps}R(\hat\theta)\geq{\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*+\sigma^2\tr(C)$, with $B,C$ as in LP450.2.
nodes.statement_clean: Algebraic identity-plus-inequality giving the bias-variance decomposition.
assumptions: Setting of DP450.1, AssumP450.1; $\hat\theta$ from DP450.2

nodes.name: Subgaussian quadratic form (Hanson-Wright variant)
nodes.section: Appendix A: Proof of Lemma bv
nodes.statement: If $\eps_1,\dots,\eps_n$ are conditionally independent given $X$ and conditionally $\sigma^2$-subgaussian, and $M$ is a.s. p.s.d., then a.s. on $X$ w.p. $\geq 1-e^{-t}$: $\bs{\eps}^\top M\bs{\eps}\leq\sigma^2\tr(M)+2\sigma^2\|M\|t+2\sigma^2\sqrt{\|M\|^2 t^2+\tr(M^2)t}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Tail bound for quadratic forms in conditionally subgaussian noise.

nodes.name: Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury identity
nodes.statement: If $k<n$, $A\in\Re^{n\times n}$ invertible, and $ZZ^\top+A$ invertible, then $Z^\top(ZZ^\top+A)^{-2}Z=(I+Z^\top A^{-1}Z)^{-1}Z^\top A^{-2}Z(I+Z^\top A^{-1}Z)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_clean: An algebraic identity used to rewrite $\tr(C)$ in terms of $A_{-i}$.

nodes.name: Square of subgaussian is subexponential
nodes.section: Appendix C: Proof of concentration inequalities
nodes.statement: For centered unit-variance $\sigma^2$-subgaussian $\xi$, $\xi^2-1$ is centered $c\sigma^2$-subexponential: $\E\exp(\lambda(\xi^2-1))\leq\exp(c^2\sigma^4\lambda^2)$ for $|\lambda|\leq 1/(c\sigma^2)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard fact relating subgaussian and subexponential norms.

nodes.name: Bernstein's inequality for subexponentials
nodes.section: Appendix C: Proof of concentration inequalities
nodes.statement: For independent mean-zero $\sigma$-subexponential $\xi_1,\dots,\xi_N$ and $a\in\Re^N$: $\Pr(|\sum_i a_i\xi_i|>t)\leq 2\exp[-c\min(t^2/(\sigma^2\sum a_i^2),t/(\sigma\max|a_i|))]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical Bernstein inequality for sums of independent subexponentials.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-net norm bound
nodes.section: Appendix C: Proof of concentration inequalities
nodes.statement: For symmetric $A\in\Re^{n\times n}$ and an $\epsilon$-net $\Nc_\epsilon$ on $\Sc^{n-1}$ with $\epsilon<1/2$: $\|A\|\leq(1-\epsilon)^{-2}\max_{x\in\Nc_\epsilon}|x^\top Ax|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard $\epsilon$-net argument for the operator norm of a symmetric matrix.

nodes.name: Courant-Fischer-Weyl variational characterization
nodes.statement: For symmetric $n\times n$ $A$ and $i\in[n]$, $\mu_i(A)$ is the minimum over subspaces $U\subseteq\Re^n$ of dimension $n-i$ of the maximum of $u^\top Au$ over unit vectors $u\in U$.
nodes.statement_clean: Min-max variational characterization of eigenvalues (one direction of the CFW theorem).

nodes.name: Monotonicity of eigenvalues
nodes.statement: If symmetric $A,B$ satisfy $A\preceq B$, then $\mu_i(A)\leq\mu_i(B)$ for all $i\in[n]$.
nodes.statement_clean: PSD ordering implies coordinatewise eigenvalue ordering.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of $\phi(k)=k/(b^2 n)+n/R_k$
nodes.statement: $1/R_{k+1}=(1/R_k-1/r_k^2)/(1-(2-1/r_k)/r_k)$, and $\phi(k+1)>\phi(k)$ whenever $r_k>bn\geq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Recurrence for $1/R_k$ and resulting monotonicity of the bound $k/(b^2 n)+n/R_k$.
conclusions: Recurrence for $1/R_{k+1}$ and strict monotonicity of $\phi$

nodes.name: Existence of summable sequence with prescribed effective ranks
nodes.statement: For any positive sequence $\{u_i\}$ with each $u_i>1$ and $\sum u_i^{-1}=\infty$, there is a unique (up to constant) positive summable sequence $\{\lambda_i\}$ with $r_i\equiv u_i$, given by $\lambda_k=u_{k-1}^{-1}\prod_{i=0}^{k-2}(1-u_i^{-1})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Characterizes which sequences of effective ranks $r_i$ can arise from summable eigenvalue sequences.

nodes.name: Equivalence of $k^*(n)/n\to 0$ and $r_n/n\to\infty$
nodes.statement: For $k^*(n)=\min\{k:r_k\geq bn\}$ with $\{r_n\}$ increasing: $k^*(n)/n\to 0$ iff $r_n/n\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Connects asymptotic effective rank growth to vanishing $k^*/n$.

nodes.name: Sufficient condition for $n/R_{k^*(n)}\to 0$
nodes.statement: If $\{r_i\}$ is increasing and $r_n/n\to\infty$, then a sufficient condition for $n/R_{k^*(n)}\to 0$ is $r_k^{-2}=o(r_k^{-1}-r_{k+1}^{-1})$ as $k\to\infty$. This holds e.g. for $r_n=n\log n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gives a discrete-derivative condition on $r_k$ guaranteeing $n/R_{k^*}$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Expanded eigenvalue benignness theorem
nodes.statement: Four parts: (1) $\lambda_{k,n}=k^{-\alpha}\ln^{-\beta}(k+1)$ benign iff $\alpha=1,\beta>1$; (2) $\lambda_{k,n}=k^{-(1+\alpha_n)}$ benign iff $\omega(1/n)=\alpha_n=o(1)$ with $R(\hat\theta)=\Theta(\min\{1/(\alpha_n n)+\alpha_n,1\})$; (3) truncated $\lambda_{k,n}=k^{-\alpha}$ for $k\leq p_n$ benign iff $0<\alpha<1, p_n=\omega(n), p_n=o(n^{1/(1-\alpha)})$ or $\alpha=1, p_n=e^{\omega(\sqrt{n})}, p_n=e^{o(n)}$; (4) truncated exponential plus constant: same as in TP450.2 part (2).
nodes.statement_clean: Expanded version of TP450.2 with two additional families of eigenvalue patterns.
conclusions: Conditions for benignness in four eigenvalue families
Sharp risk rate for the polynomial-with-shifting-exponent family

nodes.name: Bias upper bound
nodes.section: Appendix H: Upper bound on $B$ term
nodes.statement: There is $c$ depending only on $\sigma_x$ such that for any $1<t<n$, w.p. $\geq 1-e^{-t}$: ${\theta^*}^\top B\theta^*\leq c\|\theta^*\|^2\|\Sigma\|\max\{\sqrt{r_0(\Sigma)/n},r_0(\Sigma)/n,\sqrt{t/n}\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: High-probability bound on the bias term using Koltchinskii's covariance estimation theorem.

nodes.name: Proof of LP450.21
nodes.section: Appendix H: Upper bound on $B$ term
nodes.statement: Use $(I-X^\top(XX^\top)^{-1}X)X^\top=0$ and the projection norm bound, then invoke Theorem 9 of Koltchinskii-Lounici 2017 to bound $\|\Sigma-X^\top X/n\|$.

nodes.name: Block index sets $S_j$
nodes.statement: $S_1=\{1\}$; for $j>1$, $S_j=\{i_{j-1},\dots,i_j\}$ with $i_j$ the least index s.t. $\sum_{i\in S_j}\lambda_i\geq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Partition of indices into blocks whose eigenvalue mass is $\geq 1$ each.

nodes.name: Number of blocks $d$
nodes.statement: $d$ equals the (finite) number of $S_j$'s if finite, otherwise $d=\lceil n\ln n\rceil$.

nodes.name: Algorithm $C$ (quantization-based reduction)
nodes.statement: Given $(x,y)$, draw artificial noise $\eps\sim N(0,1)$ and $\zeta\sim U(-\alpha/2,\alpha/2)$, then feed $(x, y+Q_\alpha(\eps)+\zeta)$ to the least-norm interpolant $A$, where $Q_\alpha$ rounds to the nearest multiple of $\alpha$.
nodes.statement_clean: Wraps the least-norm interpolant with quantized artificial noise to enable a packing-based lower bound.
output: Estimator $\hat\theta$ such that $\rho(\hat\theta,\theta^*)$ can be lower bounded

nodes.name: Block partition has $\Omega(n\log n)$ sets
nodes.statement: Definition DP450.6 produces $\Omega(n\log n)$ sets when $r_0/(n\log(1+r_0))\geq c_2$.

nodes.name: $\rho$-distance dominates $\ell_2$ on block-constant lift
nodes.statement: For all $u,v\in\Re^d$, $\rho(\phi(u),\phi(v))\geq\|u-v\|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lifting an $\ell_2$ packing through $\phi$ produces a $\rho$-packing.

nodes.name: Reduction from interpolant error to quantized-input error
nodes.statement: If algorithm $A$ has $\rho$-error $\tau$ from $n$ samples drawn from $N(0,\Sigma)$ with independent $N(0,1)$ noise w.p. $1-\delta$, and $\alpha\leq\min\{\delta/(2n),2\tau\}$, then noise-free Algorithm $C$ given $(x,Q_\alpha(\theta^\top x))$ achieves $\rho(\hat\theta,\theta^*)^2\leq\tau$ w.p. $1-2\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Total-variation reduction from the noisy least-norm setting to a quantized noiseless setting.
assumptions: $A$ has error $\tau$ from $N(0,\Sigma)$ data with $N(0,1)$ noise w.p. $1-\delta$
conclusions: Algorithm $C$ on quantized noiseless inputs achieves $\rho(\hat\theta,\theta^*)^2\leq\tau$ w.p. $1-2\delta$

nodes.name: TV approximation via quantization
nodes.statement: (a) For $\eta\sim N(0,1)$, $\zeta\sim U(-\alpha/2,\alpha/2)$: TV distance between law of $y+\eta$ and law of $Q_\alpha(y+\eta)+\zeta$ is $\leq\alpha$. (b) TV between law of $Q_\alpha(y+\eta)$ and law of $Q_\alpha(y)+Q_\alpha(\eta)$ is $\leq\alpha$.
conclusions: TV bounds (a) and (b) on quantized Gaussian variables

nodes.name: Product distribution TV bound
nodes.statement: For probability distributions $P_1,\dots,P_n,Q_1,\dots,Q_n$ on $U$ and $[0,1]$-valued random variable $\chi$ on $U^n$: $|\E_{\prod P_t}\chi - \E_{\prod Q_t}\chi|\leq\sum_t d_{TV}(P_t,Q_t)$.
conclusions: TV inequality for products of distributions

nodes.name: Tail bound on $\|x_t\|$
nodes.statement: For each row $x_t$ of $X$ and $q>1$: $\Pr(\|x_t\|>q\sqrt{s})\leq\exp(-q^2/c)$, where $s=\sum_i\lambda_i$.

nodes.name: Lower bound via covering on quantized regression
nodes.statement: If $1/\alpha=O(n)$, there is a constant $\tau$ such that for any regression algorithm $C$ given $n$ examples $(X,Q_\alpha(X\theta^*))$ with rows of $X$ i.i.d. $N(0,\Sigma)$, w.p. $\geq 1/2$ the output $\hat\theta$ satisfies $\rho(\hat\theta,\theta^*)^2>\tau$.
nodes.statement_clean: Information-theoretic packing lower bound that quantized noiseless regression cannot solve too accurately.

nodes.name: Connection to neural tangent kernel and benign overfitting in deep nets
nodes.statement: Wide neural networks trained from suitable random initialization can be approximated linearly via the neural tangent kernel; the eigenvalues of the NTK can have heavy tails, suggesting that high-but-finite-dimensional spaces with slowly decaying eigenvalues are the relevant regime, though Theorem $\ref{th::main}$'s assumption that random covariates are linearly transformed independent components fails for the NTK.

nodes.name: Extending benign-overfitting characterization to deep neural networks
nodes.statement: Confirm that truncating to a finite-dimensional space is important for good statistical performance in the overfitting regime of deep networks, by extending the linear regression characterization to nonlinearly parameterized function classes such as neural networks.

nodes.name: Misspecified setting and relaxed covariate assumptions
nodes.statement: Determine whether the benign-overfitting characterization holds when $\E[y|x]$ is not linear, and to what extent the assumption that $x$ is a linear function of independent random variables (which excludes infinite-dimensional RKHSs with continuous kernels on finite-dimensional spaces) can be relaxed.
